rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` has the front matter that marks a bundled skill, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.next`.

The requirement says the workflow must end by naming the skill for the next task. The last workflow step, "7. Next, follow the habeas-evidence skill to author evidence and fix what it reports", does that. It names `habeas-evidence` and also points to its "Disagreeing assessments" section for the case where assessments disagree.

The workflow has one other exit. In step 5, a design session with no code to write stops there. That outcome leads to no further task, so the requirement lets it name no skill.

The other skills the text mentions are `habeas-refactor` and `habeas-evidence`, in the description and in the notes on renaming or moving requirements. They are not workflow outcomes, so the requirement does not call for them at the end.

The site meets the obligation. There was no violation-query match to judge.

text: Each bundled skill's workflow MUST end by naming the bundled skill for the next task, or, when different outcomes lead to different tasks, the skill for each such outcome. An outcome that leads to no further task needs no skill named. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
